subject: Acceptance criteria & exit gates for CardioSense evaluation
messages:
From: Mike Green <mike.green@cardiosense.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Lopez <nina.lopez@cardiosense.io>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance criteria & exit gates for CardioSense evaluation

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a two-week eval window starting May 11 and need to lock down what 'pass' looks like so procurement can sign off. High-level asks from our side:

- Clear functional acceptance tests (accuracy/perf) for the three main flows: OCR ingestion, clinical note summarization, and user-facing triage prompts.
- SLAs for latency under our expected concurrency (20 concurrent agents during clinic hours).
- Clear rollback/escape criteria if model regressions appear.
- Evidence artifacts we can hand to security/procurement (logs, KV retention policy).

Can you propose an acceptance test matrix and who owns each test? Procurement would like the MAP and test artifacts attached to the SOW.

Also copying Nina (head of clinical ops) — she may add a couple of clinical success checks.

Thanks,
Mike
Head of Product, CardioSense
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Green <mike.green@cardiosense.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance criteria & exit gates for CardioSense evaluation

Mike — great notes, thanks. Attached is a lean MAP (MAP_CardioSense_v2.xlsx) and a first-pass acceptance_test_matrix.csv that maps flows to pass/fail gates and evidence. Summary below (we can iterate):

1) Primary success signals (must be met to 'pass' eval)
- Clinical summarization F1 >= 0.82 on CardioSense gold set (owner: Product/CS)
- OCR ingestion error rate < 0.5% across 1,000 scanned docs (owner: Ops)
- Triage prompt top intent match >= 92% on sampled prompts (owner: Clinical Ops)
- 95th percentile latency < 600ms for single-turn user prompt at target concurrency (owner: Infra/Redwood)

2) Exit gates (conditions that block production rollforward)
- Any single regression >8% relative drop on F1 vs baseline on core summary metric
- Reproducible data leakage or PII exposure in generated responses
- More than 1 unplanned downtime incident >5 minutes during the eval window

3) Acceptance tests and evidence (examples)
- Test: batch run of 500 annotated notes, produce per-case precision/recall; Evidence: CSV of predictions + scoring script + raw dataset subset (anonymized)
- Test: concurrency load test with synthetic traffic to validate 95th pctl latency; Evidence: tracing logs, flamegraph, per-token timing CSV
- Test: KV cache correctness smoke-run for long-running sessions; Evidence: annotated session traces

4) Owners and handoffs
- Redwood will own infra/latency verification and provide exported traces + sampling of full request/response payloads (redacted).
- CardioSense owns clinical validation; we will pair on the scoring harness and provide a reproducible evaluation notebook.
- Procurement needs MAP attached to SOW and a short evidence bundle for SOC/IT review.

Next steps request from our side:
- Confirm the 3 clinical acceptance metrics and provide sample gold data by May 6 so we can generate the scoring runs before May 11.
- Tell us which evidence items procurement *must* receive (we'll assemble).

Attachments: MAP_CardioSense_v2.xlsx (MAP table), acceptance_test_matrix.csv (detailed checks).

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Looping in a couple technical clarifications from infra/serving:

- Latency target: 95th pctl < 600ms for single-turn is achievable, but we need to confirm payload sizes used in your sampling (avg tokens per prompt & response). If average response is ~120 tokens we hit ~450-520ms on an rtx-based Dedicated slice; if it's 300 tokens we'll need to tune batching/kv cache.

- Concurrency: our load tests will simulate 20 agents with Poisson arrival; confirm if the 20 is sustained for clinic hours or bursty spikes (helps set autoscale/burst policy).

- Acceptance thresholds and rollback: suggest two-tiered rollback triggers:
  * Soft alert: single metric drop between 5-8% -> automatic canary rollback + priority investigation (no customer-impactful switch yet).
  * Hard fail: >8% drop or PII hit -> immediate cut to fallback model and trigger incident review.

Action items from Redwood infra (owner: Karthik):
- Produce a reproducible load script and a test run report by May 8.
- Provide an anonymized sample trace for your team to verify payload sizing.

Mike, could you reply with a line stating typical response length and whether concurrency is sustained or bursty? Also tagging Ben for legal/procurement artifacts he can prep.

Thanks,
Karthik
Technical Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah / Karthik — that all looks reasonable. Quick answers:

- Typical response length: 90–140 tokens (most notes are concise), occasionally up to 220 tokens.
- Concurrency pattern: sustained during clinic windows (08:00–17:00 local), with short spikes up to +40% at shift changes.

We confirm the three clinical metrics and will share a 250-note de-identified gold set by May 6 EOD (Nina). We also need a one-page evidence packet for procurement listing: logs (last 30 days synthetic), SOC2 artifact pointer, KV retention policy summary, and the MAP attached to the SOW.

Ben — can you produce the evidence packet and a short SOW-friendly blurb for legal review? Also, can Redwood provide a DocuSign link so procurement signs the MAP+SOW this week?

Once we have the load script and the scoring runs from you, we can finalize the go/no-go checklist.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — excited to kick this off.

Mike
Head of Product, CardioSense
